evidence.claim: Model risk score 0.77. In the 0.70-0.85 band the bank's closed history holds 817 confirmed frauds against 234 cleared alarms, a likelihood ratio of 0.67 - mildly exculpatory, consistent with the dataset note that above 0.70 most flagged transactions turn out to be legitimate

The identity record marks this device New for the account. 83% of cleared alarms had a New device against 18% of confirmed fraud: on its own a new device is the signature of a cardholder who has just bought a phone, not of a compromise
The card has no billing history in region 327.0, but every card-detail match flag passed. 716 of the 900 alarms the bank cleared were exactly this: a cardholder travelling, confirmed on contact

$599.94 is 6.0x this card's median and above its 95th percentile. Counter-intuitively this is mildly exculpatory: large outliers appear on 16% of cleared alarms and 6% of confirmed fraud, because confirmed fraud tends to stay inside the cardholder's normal range to avoid attention
The bank has 2 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-3886, CC-0615), pattern(s): card_not_present_new_device

External email-domain intelligence classifies 'anonymous.com' as a masked address -- the processor withheld it rather than the cardholder choosing an anonymous one. Measured against the bank's closed cases that points away from fraud (log-likelihood ratio -1.39). The domain is in the transaction; what kind of domain it is, is not -- that is the one piece of evidence here the institution does not own.

Connected components place this card in the graph's giant device-sharing component (2,500 cards). Transitive device sharing percolates at every threshold tested, so membership is not evidence of a ring and carries no weight here; it is recorded because policy R6 asks for the shared element to be named.

Known fraud pattern 3: Card-not-present fraud from a new device: Card-not-present fraud from a new device. Same as above, with the identity record marking the device as `New` for this account, sometimes behind a proxy. Stronger than pattern 2, still not proof: people buy new phones.

evidence.claim: Fraud Policy - 6. Stopping: Stop investigating when one of these holds: - Fraud probability is at or above 0.85, or at or below 0.15, supported by at least two independent pieces of evidence - A verification response settles the question - Further steps are unlikely to change the decision. Say so in `stop_reason` Investigations that continue past a defensible decision waste time. Investigations that stop before one create risk.
